newsitem.title: USA: Applied Materials Q1 new orders rise.
newsitem.headline: Applied Materials Q1 new orders rise.

text.p: Applied Materials Inc Tuesday said new orders for the first quarter of fiscal 1997 rose 32.4 percent to $904.7 million from $683.2 million in the fourth quarter of fiscal 1996.

In a statement, Applied Materials, which makes the equipment that makes semiconductors, attributed the increase in new orders to strategic purchases by customers in Japan, Korea and Taiwan. North American orders were 28 percent of the company's total, Japan was 24 percent, Asia-Pacific was 23 percent, Korea 15 percent and Europe 10 percent.
Included in the first quarter orders was a $105 million order from Korean-based Anam Group's Anam Industrial Co Ltd., for semiconductor production systems.
Applied Materials said backlog at the end of the first quarter of fiscal 1997 was $1.4 billion, even with its backlog at the end of fiscal 1996.

"Looking forward, we see a growing long-term demand for semiconductor manufacturing equipment as semiconductor devices become more complex and their applications expand," the company said. "For the remainder of fiscal 1997, we expect demand for production equipment from logic and microprocessor manufacturers to continue to strengthen, and memory capacity investment to remain selective until later in this cycle as excess capacity is absorbed."
Earlier, Applied Materials reported a first quarter profit of $29.6 million or $0.16 a share on sales of $835.8 million, including a pre-tax charge of $59.5 million or $0.32 a share.
Excluding the charge, the profit translated into earnings of $0..48 a share compared with a First Call consensus of $0.44.
In the year-ago quarter, Applied Materials earned $171.6 million or $0.93 a share on sales of $1.04 billion.
